concept.title: Who can see your tree
concept.shortdesc: Your tree is yours: you decide who gets a copy, and your keeps it safe.

conbody.p: Your tree is yours. does not send it anywhere. Nobody who makes can see it.
You decide what goes in your tree, where you keep it and who gets a copy. That makes you the data controller for the people in it. This includes any who are still alive.

section.title: Copies that Android makes
section.p: Android has its own way to back up your . If it is on, Android may copy the files of apps to your Google account. Your trees go with them.
Android makes this copy, not . It is kept under your own account. Nobody who makes can see it.
To see whether it is on, open the Settings app and search for backup. You can turn it off there.

section.title: Copies that you save
section.p: A copy that you save goes where you choose. shows how. A folder that is kept in step with a service, such as Google Drive or Dropbox, sends that service a copy too. It keeps it under your account.

section.title: Your files are not locked by
section.p: does not encrypt your trees. They are ordinary files. What keeps them safe is your .
Android encrypts the files on your , and your screen lock is the key. Keep a PIN, a pattern or a password on it.
If you give someone a copy of a tree, they can read all of it.

section.title: Pictures from a website
section.p: A tree can point to a picture on a website. says what that website can see, and where the picture is kept.
